enum/DataStoreRequestType.d:
Categorizes data store operations for use with DataStoreService:GetRequestBudgetForRequestType(), which returns the remaining per-server request budget for a given category.

The enum contains two sets of values. The legacy values (GetAsync, SetIncrementAsync, UpdateAsync, GetSortedAsync, SetIncrementSortedAsync, OnUpdate, ListAsync, GetVersionAsync, and RemoveVersionAsync) should not be used. The modern values (StandardRead, StandardWrite, StandardList, StandardRemove, OrderedRead, OrderedWrite, OrderedList, and OrderedRemove) correspond to the newer DataStore and OrderedDataStore API families that use universe-level and per-server limits.

enum/DistanceAttenuationMode.d: Determines how an AudioEmitter attenuates (fades out) as the distance between the AudioEmitter and an interacting AudioListener increases. Most values refer to a preset rolloff curve that the AudioEmitter will apply over the range given by DistanceAttenuationBounds. When set to DistanceAttenuationMode.Custom, the emitter instead uses a developer-supplied curve given by AudioEmitter:SetDistanceAttenuation().
enum/DistanceAttenuationMode.s: Determines how an `Class.AudioEmitter` attenuates (fades out) as the distance between the `Class.AudioEmitter` and an interacting `Class.AudioListener` increases.

m.d: Uses the developer-supplied DistanceAttenuation curve for gain rolloff.
m.s: Uses the developer-supplied `Class.AudioEmitter.DistanceAttenuation|DistanceAttenuation` curve for gain rolloff.

m.d: Volume attenuates according to a hybrid model which follows the DistanceAttenuationMode.Inverse model when close to the lower bound of AudioEmitter.DistanceAttenuationBounds and the DistanceAttenuationMode.LinearSquared model when close to the upper bound of AudioEmitter.DistanceAttenuationBounds. This is done by taking the lesser of these two curves, such that the curve mostly follows an inverse relationship but tapers to silence at the maximum distance.
m.s: Volume attenuates according to a hybrid model which follows the `Enum.DistanceAttenuationMode.Inverse` model when close to the lower bound of `Class.AudioEmitter.DistanceAttenuationBounds` and the `Enum.DistanceAttenuationMode.LinearSquared` model when close to the upper bound of `Class.AudioEmitter.DistanceAttenuationBounds`. This is done by taking the lesser of these two curves, such that the curve mostly follows an inverse relationship but tapers to silence at the maximum distance.

m.d: Volume attenuates between the bounds of AudioEmitter.DistanceAttenuationBounds with a linear relationship. This is done by computing (maxDistance - distance) / (maxDistance - minDistance), where distance is the Vector3.Magnitude between the AudioEmitter's position and the AudioListener's position.
m.s: Volume attenuates between the bounds of `Class.AudioEmitter.DistanceAttenuationBounds` with a linear relationship. This is done by computing (`maxDistance` - `distance`) / (`maxDistance` - `minDistance`), where distance is the `Class.Vector3.Magnitude` between the `Class.AudioEmitter`'s position and the `Class.AudioListener`'s position.

m.d: Volume attenuates between the bounds of AudioEmitter.DistanceAttenuationBounds with a linear-squared relationship. This is done by squaring the formula used to determine the volume when using DistanceAttenuationMode.Linear, which creates a parabolic curve with a steeper fade.
m.s: Volume attenuates between the bounds of `Class.AudioEmitter.DistanceAttenuationBounds` with a linear-squared relationship. This is done by squaring the formula used to determine the volume when using `Enum.DistanceAttenuationMode.Linear`, which creates a parabolic curve with a steeper fade.

m.d: Volume attenuates from the lower bound of AudioEmitter.DistanceAttenuationBounds in an inverse manner, mirroring how sounds attenuate in the real world. This is done by computing (minDistance/distance), where distance is the Vector2.Magnitude between the AudioEmitter's position and the AudioListener's position.
m.s: Volume attenuates from the lower bound of `Class.AudioEmitter.DistanceAttenuationBounds` in an inverse manner, mirroring how sounds attenuate in the real world. This is done by computing (`minDistance`/`distance`), where `distance` is the `Class.Vector2.Magnitude` between the `Class.AudioEmitter`'s position and the `Class.AudioListener`'s position.

enum/FilterErrorType.d:
FilterErrorType classifies each FilterError returned when the Studio Explorer filter bar cannot parse or validate a filter expression. A FilterError carries the type alongside the source range and human-readable message so tooling can distinguish failure categories programmatically.

Values fall into three groups:

  • Lexer errors — the raw character stream cannot be tokenized.
  • Parser errors — a valid token stream forms an invalid expression tree.
  • Bespoke-filter and property errors — the expression is syntactically valid but semantically incorrect (unknown property, unsupported type, bad operator, and similar).
enum/FilterErrorType.s: Identifies the category of a parse or validation error produced by the Studio Explorer filter expression engine.

m.d: A backslash at the end of a quoted string has nothing after it to escape.
m.s: A backslash at the end of a quoted string has nothing after it to escape.

m.d: A recognized bespoke filter keyword (such as classname:) is missing its required value, or a query: expression contains an invalid query string.
m.s: A recognized bespoke filter keyword (such as `classname:`) is missing its required value, or a `query:` expression contains an invalid query string.

m.d: An unexpected token was encountered where a name or identifier was expected.
m.s: An unexpected token was encountered where a name or identifier was expected.

m.d: Reserved error code for an incomplete or expression; currently not emitted by the filter engine.
m.s: Reserved error code for an incomplete `or` expression; currently not emitted by the filter engine.

m.d: An opening parenthesis ( in the filter expression has no matching closing parenthesis ).
m.s: An opening parenthesis `(` in the filter expression has no matching closing parenthesis `)`.

m.d: A ** wildcard token directly follows a * wildcard in a dotted name path (for example, A.*.**.X), which is not allowed.
m.s: A `**` wildcard token directly follows a `*` wildcard in a dotted name path (for example, `A.*.**.X`), which is not allowed.

m.d: A lone ~ character was found that is not part of the ~= not-equal operator.
m.s: A lone `~` character was found that is not part of the `~=` not-equal operator.

m.d: A comparison operator other than = or ~= was used with a property type that only supports equality comparisons.
m.s: A comparison operator other than `=` or `~=` was used with a property type that only supports equality comparisons.

m.d: The named property does not exist on any reflected class known to the filter engine.
m.s: The named property does not exist on any reflected class known to the filter engine.

m.d: A sub-field index (such as .W) was used with a vector or color property that does not have a field by that name.
m.s: A sub-field index (such as `.W`) was used with a vector or color property that does not have a field by that name.

m.d: The value string provided for a property comparison cannot be parsed into the expected type for that property (for example, Locked=notabool).
m.s: The value string provided for a property comparison cannot be parsed into the expected type for that property (for example, `Locked=notabool`).

m.d: A sub-field index was used with a property type that does not support field access (for example, Locked.X=true).
m.s: A sub-field index was used with a property type that does not support field access (for example, `Locked.X=true`).

m.d: The named property exists but its type is not supported by the filter engine (for example, complex datatypes such as CFrame or TweenInfo).
m.s: The named property exists but its type is not supported by the filter engine (for example, complex datatypes such as `CFrame` or `TweenInfo`).

m.d: A . in a dotted name path is not followed by a valid name, number, or wildcard token.
m.s: A `.` in a dotted name path is not followed by a valid name, number, or wildcard token.

m.d: A token that cannot be a value (such as an operator) appears where a value is expected after a comparison operator.
m.s: A token that cannot be a value (such as an operator) appears where a value is expected after a comparison operator.

m.d: An and or or binary operator appears with no right-hand operand.
m.s: An `and` or `or` binary operator appears with no right-hand operand.

m.d: A quoted string was opened but not closed before the end of the filter input.
m.s: A quoted string was opened but not closed before the end of the filter input.

m.d: A name:value token uses a keyword that is not a recognized bespoke filter type (for example, foo:Bar).
m.s: A `name:value` token uses a keyword that is not a recognized bespoke filter type (for example, `foo:Bar`).

m.d: A wildcard (* or **) appears in the property portion of a dotted expression where a concrete property name is required.
m.s: A wildcard (`*` or `**`) appears in the property portion of a dotted expression where a concrete property name is required.

enum/IKCollisionsMode.d:
Controls which parts in the workspace participate in collision resolution when WorldRoot:IKMoveTo() drives a part toward a target CFrame via inverse kinematics.

The three IKCollisionsMode values offer a spectrum of collision fidelity. IKCollisionsMode.NoCollisions ignores the rest of the workspace and moves only the mechanism being dragged (fastest, most permissive). IKCollisionsMode.OtherMechanismsAnchored keeps the dragged mechanism physically correct against the scene but treats other objects as immovable anchors. IKCollisionsMode.IncludeContactedMechanisms lets the dragged mechanism push unanchored objects, so the entire contacted set participates in resolution.

WorldRoot:IKMoveTo() defaults to IKCollisionsMode.OtherMechanismsAnchored when no collisions mode is supplied.

enum/ImageCombineType.d:
Enum for determining how two images are combined together.

In all combine operations, source refers to the new pixels being drawn and destination refers to the existing pixels in the image being drawn onto.
enum/ImageCombineType.s: Enum for determining how two images are combined together.

m.d: Blends pixels from the source with pixels from the destination using source over alpha blending.
m.s: Blends pixels from the source with pixels from the destination using source over alpha blending.

m.d: Overwrites all pixels in the destination image with pixels from the source image.
m.s: Overwrites all pixels in the destination image with pixels from the source image.

m.d: Adds pixels from the source and pixels from the destination together. Source RGB values are scaled by the source alpha, while source alpha is added directly to destination alpha.
m.s: Adds pixels from the source and pixels from the destination together. Source RGB values are scaled by the source alpha, while source alpha is added directly to destination alpha.

m.d: Multiplies pixels from the source and pixels from the destination together. RGBA values are multiplied as values between 0 and 1. Values lower than 1 have a darkening effect on the image.
m.s: Multiplies pixels from the source and pixels from the destination together. RGBA values are multiplied as values between `0` and `1`. Values lower than `1` have a darkening effect on the image.

m.d: Blends pixels from the source with pixels from the destination based on the alpha of the source pixels. Unlike BlendSourceOver, the destination color in AlphaBlend affects the resulting color of the image, regardless of the destination color's alpha.
m.s: Blends pixels from the source with pixels from the destination based on the alpha of the source pixels. Unlike **BlendSourceOver**, the destination color in **AlphaBlend** affects the resulting color of the image, regardless of the destination color's alpha.

m.d: Blends pixels from the source with the destination using alpha blending, then renormalizes the resulting RGB values as a tangent-space normal vector.
m.s: Blends pixels from the source with the destination using alpha blending, then renormalizes the resulting RGB values as a tangent-space normal vector.

m.d: Subtracts pixels of the source from pixels of the destination. Source RGB values are scaled by the source alpha, while source alpha is subtracted directly from destination alpha.
m.s: Subtracts pixels of the source from pixels of the destination. Source RGB values are scaled by the source alpha, while source alpha is subtracted directly from destination alpha.

enum/InputActionType.d: This enum is used by InputAction.Type to determine which input data type the InputAction will receive.
enum/InputActionType.s: This enum is used by `Class.InputAction.Type` to determine which input data type the `Class.InputAction` will receive.

m.d: The InputAction will receive boolean values from button inputs, for example true/false on press/release from inputs such as KeyCode.ButtonA or KeyCode.E. This setting also exposes the UIButton property on child InputBindings, allowing you to easily hook up press or release of a GuiButton for the action.
m.s: The `Class.InputAction` will receive boolean values from button inputs, for example `true`/`false` on press/release from inputs such as `Enum.KeyCode.ButtonA` or `Enum.KeyCode.E`. This setting also exposes the `Class.InputBinding.UIButton|UIButton` property on child `Class.InputBinding|InputBindings`, allowing you to easily hook up press or release of a `Class.GuiButton` for the action.

m.d: The InputAction will receive numerical values, generally from analog gamepad triggers such as KeyCode.ButtonL2 or KeyCode.ButtonR2. This setting also exposes the Up and Down properties on child InputBindings, allowing for boolean inputs or "1D" inputs as composite directions for the action.
m.s: The `Class.InputAction` will receive numerical values, generally from analog gamepad triggers such as `Enum.KeyCode.ButtonL2` or `Enum.KeyCode.ButtonR2`. This setting also exposes the `Class.InputBinding.Up|Up` and `Class.InputBinding.Down|Down` properties on child `Class.InputBinding|InputBindings`, allowing for boolean inputs or "1D" inputs as composite directions for the action.

m.d: The InputAction will receive Vector2 values, generally from thumbstick inputs such as KeyCode.Thumbstick1 and KeyCode.Thumbstick2. This setting also exposes the Up, Down, Left, and Right properties on child InputBindings, allowing for "2D" inputs as composite directions for the action.
m.s: The `Class.InputAction` will receive `Datatype.Vector2` values, generally from thumbstick inputs such as `Enum.KeyCode.Thumbstick1` and `Enum.KeyCode.Thumbstick2`. This setting also exposes the `Class.InputBinding.Up|Up`, `Class.InputBinding.Down|Down`, `Class.InputBinding.Left|Left`, and `Class.InputBinding.Right|Right` properties on child `Class.InputBinding|InputBindings`, allowing for "2D" inputs as composite directions for the action.

m.d: The InputAction will receive Vector3 values from inputs assigned to the Up, Down, Left, Right, Forward, and/or Backward properties on child InputBindings, allowing for "3D" inputs as composite directions for the action.
m.s: The `Class.InputAction` will receive `Datatype.Vector3` values from inputs assigned to the `Class.InputBinding.Up|Up`, `Class.InputBinding.Down|Down`, `Class.InputBinding.Left|Left`, `Class.InputBinding.Right|Right`, `Class.InputBinding.Forward|Forward`, and/or `Class.InputBinding.Backward|Backward` properties on child `Class.InputBinding|InputBindings`, allowing for "3D" inputs as composite directions for the action.

m.s: The `Class.InputAction` will receive `Datatype.Vector2` values representing the absolute pixel (**X**, **Y**) coordinates of a pointer input in the viewport.

enum/IntermediateMeshGenerationResult.d:
IntermediateMeshGenerationResult is returned as the first argument to the optional intermediate-result callback supplied to GenerateMeshAsync(). When the backend finishes producing an intermediate version of the mesh before the final result is ready, the callback fires with a value from this enum together with a generationId string and a contextId string. enum/KeyCodeStringFormat.d: This enum is used with UserInputService:GetStringForKeyCode() to control how the returned key string is formatted. The Abbreviated option provides shortened labels suitable for compact UI elements such as keybind hints, tooltips, or on-screen button prompts where space is limited.
enum/KeyCodeStringFormat.s: Determines the string format returned by `Class.UserInputService:GetStringForKeyCode()`.

m.d: Default behavior which returns the full key string, for example "LeftControl", "Backspace", or "Escape".
m.s: Default behavior which returns the full key string, for example `"LeftControl"`, `"Backspace"`, or `"Escape"`.

m.d: Returns a shortened key string when available, for example "LCtrl", "Bksp", or "Esc".
m.s: Returns a shortened key string when available, for example `"LCtrl"`, `"Bksp"`, or `"Esc"`.

enum/KeyInterpolationMode.d: Describes the interpolation method for a FloatCurve or RotationCurve segment between the key for which this mode is set and the next key in the curve.
enum/KeyInterpolationMode.s: Describes the interpolation method between two keys.

m.d: The segment starting at this key will constantly evaluate to the value set at this key.
m.s: The segment starting at this key will constantly evaluate to the value set at this key.

m.d: The segment starting at this key will evaluate using a linear interpolation at this key and the value at the next key.
m.s: The segment starting at this key will evaluate using a linear interpolation at this key and the value at the next key.

m.d: The segment starting at this key will evaluate using cubic interpolation of this key value using its right tangent and the next key value and its left tangent.
m.s: The segment starting at this key will evaluate using cubic interpolation of this key value using its right tangent and the next key value and its left tangent.
